canonical_statement: The PROVE IT-TIMI 22 statin comparison tested whether standard LDL-cholesterol lowering with pravastatin 40 mg daily was noninferior to more intensive lowering with atorvastatin 80 mg daily for preventing death or major cardiovascular events after acute coronary syndrome.

concept.text: Death from any cause or major cardiovascular event

outcome.definition: First occurrence of death from any cause, myocardial infarction, documented unstable angina requiring rehospitalization, revascularization performed at least 30 days after randomization, or stroke

canonical_statement: Eligible patients were randomly assigned 1:1, in double-blind double-dummy fashion, to pravastatin 40 mg daily or atorvastatin 80 mg daily.

population.label: Adults hospitalized for an acute coronary syndrome within the preceding 10 days

canonical_statement: The statin randomization was embedded in a 2-by-2 factorial trial in which patients were also randomized to a 10-day monthly course of gatifloxacin or placebo; the antibiotic results were not reported in this article.

population.label: Adults hospitalized for an acute coronary syndrome within the preceding 10 days

canonical_statement: Between November 15, 2000, and December 22, 2001, the trial enrolled 4162 patients at 349 sites in eight countries.

population.label: Trial population enrolled at 349 sites in eight countries

canonical_statement: Eligible participants were men or women at least 18 years old who had been hospitalized within the preceding 10 days for myocardial infarction with or without ST-segment elevation or for high-risk unstable angina, were clinically stable, and were enrolled after planned percutaneous revascularization.

population.label: ACS eligibility population
inclusion_criteria: Enrollment after planned PCI if applicable

canonical_statement: The cholesterol eligibility threshold was total cholesterol 240 mg/dL or less, except that patients receiving long-term lipid-lowering therapy at the index acute coronary syndrome had to have total cholesterol 200 mg/dL or less at screening.

population.label: Cholesterol eligibility population
inclusion_criteria: If on long-term lipid-lowering therapy at index event, total cholesterol <=200 mg/dL at screening

canonical_statement: Patients were excluded if a coexisting condition shortened expected survival to less than two years, if they were receiving a statin dose of 80 mg/day at the index event, or if fibric-acid-derivative or niacin therapy could not be discontinued before randomization.

population.label: Key treatment and prognosis exclusions
exclusion_criteria: Fibrate or niacin therapy that could not be discontinued

canonical_statement: Use within the prior month, or anticipated need during the trial, for a strong cytochrome P-450 3A4 inhibitor was an exclusion criterion because atorvastatin is metabolized through that pathway.

population.label: CYP3A4-interaction exclusion
exclusion_criteria: Recent or anticipated strong CYP3A4 inhibitor therapy

canonical_statement: Patients were excluded for percutaneous coronary intervention within the previous six months other than for the qualifying event, coronary-artery bypass surgery within the previous two months, or planned bypass surgery for the index event.

population.label: Recent revascularization exclusions
exclusion_criteria: PCI within prior 6 months other than qualifying event

canonical_statement: Other exclusions included factors that might prolong the QT interval, obstructive hepatobiliary or other serious hepatic disease, unexplained creatine kinase elevation greater than three times the upper limit of normal not related to myocardial infarction, or serum creatinine greater than 2.0 mg/dL.

population.label: Other safety exclusions
exclusion_criteria: Obstructive hepatobiliary or serious hepatic disease
Unexplained CK >3x ULN not due to MI

canonical_statement: Follow-up visits with dietary counseling occurred at 30 days, 4 months, and every 4 months thereafter; lipid and safety blood samples were obtained at randomization, 30 days, 4, 8, 12, and 16 months, and the final visit.

population.label: Adults hospitalized for an acute coronary syndrome within the preceding 10 days

canonical_statement: The protocol specified blinded escalation of pravastatin to 80 mg when LDL cholesterol exceeded 125 mg/dL on two consecutive visits in adherent patients, and either study drug could be halved for abnormal liver tests, elevated creatine kinase, or myalgias.

population.label: Adults hospitalized for an acute coronary syndrome within the preceding 10 days

canonical_statement: Patients were followed for 18 to 36 months, with an average follow-up of 24 months; the trial continued until 925 endpoint events had been reported, and 8 patients (0.2%) were lost to follow-up.

population.label: Adults hospitalized for an acute coronary syndrome within the preceding 10 days

canonical_statement: The primary efficacy outcome was time from randomization to the first occurrence of death from any cause, myocardial infarction, documented unstable angina requiring rehospitalization, revascularization performed at least 30 days after randomization, or stroke.

concept.text: Death from any cause or major cardiovascular event

outcome.definition: First occurrence of death from any cause, myocardial infarction, documented unstable angina requiring rehospitalization, revascularization performed at least 30 days after randomization, or stroke

canonical_statement: Myocardial infarction required ischemic or infarction symptoms plus either new Q waves in at least two leads or cardiac-marker evidence meeting the TIMI/American College of Cardiology definition.

outcome.definition: Symptoms suggestive of ischemia or infarction plus qualifying ECG or cardiac-marker evidence

canonical_statement: Unstable angina required ischemic discomfort at rest for at least 10 minutes prompting rehospitalization plus qualifying ST-T changes, cardiac-marker elevation below the myocardial-infarction threshold, or a distinct second episode of ischemic discomfort lasting more than 10 minutes.

outcome.definition: Rest ischemic discomfort >=10 minutes prompting rehospitalization plus prespecified ECG, biomarker, or recurrent-symptom evidence

canonical_statement: Secondary endpoints included coronary-heart-disease death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or revascularization; coronary-heart-disease death or nonfatal myocardial infarction; and the individual components of the primary endpoint.
The noninferiority boundary was an upper limit of the one-sided 95% confidence interval for the two-year relative risk below 1.17, corresponding to a hazard ratio through follow-up of 1.198.

The authors concluded that, after a recent acute coronary syndrome, intensive lipid lowering with atorvastatin 80 mg provided greater protection against death or major cardiovascular events than standard lipid lowering with pravastatin 40 mg.

canonical_statement: The study could not establish the mechanism of clinical benefit and could not exclude non-lipid pleiotropic differences between atorvastatin and pravastatin as a contributor to the observed outcome difference.

The safety and efficacy findings came from a carefully selected and monitored population that excluded patients receiving strong CYP3A4 inhibitors; the authors cautioned that patients in routine practice may have more comorbidity and may tolerate high-dose statin therapy less well.

canonical_statement: The trial could not determine whether the continued longer-term benefit reflected ongoing intensive lipid lowering, an early plaque-stabilization effect, or other differences between the two statins.
